title: Massanutten Rental Watch
about: Short-term rental news for Massanutten owners from public county and association records.

county.name: Rockingham County
county.headline: Work with rental owners, in public
county.lede: Owners are asking the Board of Supervisors to treat short-term rental owners as stakeholders: talk with us, and set rental rules in public meetings with time for comment.

main_action.title: Before the November 12 work session on short-term rentals, ask the county to include owners
main_action.short: The Board of Supervisors and the Planning Commission will discuss short-term rentals together on November 12. Email them first: ask that owners be treated as stakeholders and that any rule changes go to a public hearing.
main_action.detail: The Board of Supervisors and the Planning Commission will hold a joint work session on short-term rentals on November 12. Owners are asking the county to treat them as stakeholders: meet with them, and put any change to rental rules on a public agenda with time for comment.
steps: Massanutten is in District 5, represented by Supervisor Joel Hensley. The Board page lists all five supervisors and has an Email Us link. Write to all five, and ask the Community Development office, (540) 564-3030, to pass your note to the Planning Commission.
Say who you are: a Massanutten owner who rents short term, and whether you live here.
Ask for three things: meet with rental owners before any changes are drafted, put any change to rental rules on a public hearing agenda, and allow public comment before a vote.
Keep it short and courteous, in your own words.
Work sessions usually take no public comment, so send it before November 12. The session's time and materials are not posted yet; this page will update when they are.

more_actions.title: Existing short-term rentals: apply for your county permit by December 31
more_actions.short: Every short-term rental already operating must apply by December 31. The form asks for your bedrooms and the most guests you plan to host.
more_actions.detail: Under the ordinance adopted December 10, 2025, short-term rentals already operating in Rockingham County must apply for a county permit by December 31, 2026.
steps: Download the application from the county's Short-Term Rentals page.
The form allows up to two guests per bedroom, plus four on public sewer.
Attach a site layout, a fire safety and evacuation plan with a diagram for each bedroom, proof of short-term rental liability insurance, and the fee.
The affidavit of compliance on that page is for renewing next year, not for this application.
Apply early in case the county asks for more information.

more_actions.title: Get county agendas the moment they are posted
more_actions.short: County agendas post only a few days before each meeting. Free email alerts tell you right away.
more_actions.detail: The county posts Board of Supervisors and Planning Commission agendas only a few days before each meeting. The next Board of Supervisors meeting is Wednesday, October 28 at 6 PM.
steps: Sign up for the county's free email alerts and choose the Agenda Center alerts for the Board of Supervisors and the Planning Commission.
When an agenda includes short-term rentals, speak during public comment or write to your supervisor before the meeting.

coming_up.title: Joint work session on short-term rentals (Board of Supervisors and Planning Commission)
coming_up.detail: Announced on the November 4 Planning Commission agenda. Time not posted; the Board's regular meeting that day is at 3 PM.

findings.title: Board and Planning Commission to hold a joint work session on short-term rentals November 12
findings.detail: The November 4 Planning Commission agenda lists upcoming joint work sessions with the Board of Supervisors: short-term rentals on November 12 and strategic planning on December 3. No time, materials, or agenda for the session are posted yet. Work sessions usually take no public comment, so writing beforehand is the way to be heard.

findings.title: Board denied the 10-bedroom short-term rental barn, 5 to 0
findings.detail: On October 14 the Board denied a permit to turn a barn on Resort Drive, McGaheysville, into a second dwelling with up to 10 bedrooms for short-term rental. Supervisor Hensley, who represents Massanutten, made the motion; he said the application left out maximum occupancy and that second dwellings on farm land were meant for family or farming. Chair Longcor and Supervisor Dale called the rental a commercial business in a non-commercial zone. Neighbors spoke against it. Source: the October 14 minutes in the October 28 agenda packet.

findings.title: Another approval came with a ban on short-term rentals
findings.detail: Also on October 14, the Board approved a second dwelling in Cross Keys for an aging parent, with the condition that neither house may ever be a short-term rental. Supervisor Dale proposed the condition. Supervisor Wolfe-Garrison objected that it limits property rights and sets a precedent, but the vote was 5 to 0.

findings.title: County has approved 26 short-term rental permits so far
findings.detail: The community development report in the October 28 agenda packet lists 26 approved permits. Every short-term rental already operating must apply by December 31.

findings.title: Massanutten water and sewer rates up for review in early December
findings.detail: On October 14 county staff said they have finished the promised one-year review of Massanutten Water and Sewer Authority rates and asked for a work session with the authority in early December. No date is set yet.

findings.title: Board met in closed session on litigation, with the rental administrator present
findings.detail: On October 2 the Board held a 46-minute closed meeting for consultation with legal counsel about actual or probable litigation. The county's Short-Term Rental Administrator, the zoning administrators, and the community development director attended. The minutes do not say what the litigation is.

findings.title: County updated the short-term rental application form
findings.detail: The Short Term Rental Application in the county's document center carries a new date of October 2, 2026. What changed has not been compared yet.

findings.title: Board keeps barring short-term rentals in second dwellings
findings.detail: At the September 23 meeting, applicants for a second-dwelling permit (SUP26-0903) offered a condition prohibiting short-term rentals. On July 8 the Board added the same condition to another approval by a 4 to 1 vote, at Supervisor Wolfe-Garrison's request.

association.name: Massanutten covenants
association.headline: Owners should shape the covenant rewrite
association.lede: The association is rewriting the covenants every owner lives under. No comment deadline or vote process has been posted, so comment now while changes are still possible.

main_action.title: Tell the association what you think of Covenants 1 and 19
main_action.short: Covenant 1 would ban outdoor fires without written approval. Covenant 19 adds new limits on activities, lighting, and quiet hours. Seven more sections were posted October 31, including Covenant 25 on assessments. No deadline is posted.
main_action.detail: The covenant rewrite is open for owner comment and no deadline has been posted. Two changes affect every owner. Covenant 1 would ban all outdoor fires without the association's written approval, which could cover gas fire tables, fire pits, outdoor fireplaces, and grills, and an approval could be revoked at any time. Covenant 19 adds an undefined test that activities, amenities, and lighting be consistent with a single-family home on a comparably sized lot, and lets the association set quiet hours for noise and lighting without an owner vote.
steps: Open the feedback form. Each covenant has its own comment box.

Covenant 1 box: ask that outdoor fire be defined as burning wood, brush, leaves, or trash, and campfires; that gas fire features and grills be expressly allowed; and that an approval be revocable only for cause or during an official burn ban.

Covenant 19 box: ask that the sentence about being consistent with a single-family home be removed, that quiet hours be set only after owner notice and comment, and that entry, path, and stair safety lighting be exempt.

New on October 31: read Covenants 3, 9 and 10, 12, 15, 25, 26, and 29, and use their boxes if they matter to you. Covenant 25 drops the word "reasonable" and the list of purposes from annual assessments; Covenant 9 requires approval to remove most trees.
Use your own words. Short comments from many owners carry more weight than one long letter.
The form asks for your name, Massanutten address, and email.

more_actions.title: Go to the Covenant Amendment Task Force meeting on November 19
more_actions.short: The task force now meets on its own on November 19. It is the next chance to raise Covenants 1 and 19 in person. Time and place are not posted yet.
more_actions.detail: The association's calendar moved the Covenant Amendment Task Force from a shared November 5 meeting with the Rules Committee to its own meeting on Thursday, November 19.
steps: Call the association office at (540) 289-9466 or email Mpoa@MassanuttenVillage.com to ask the time and place and whether owners may speak.
If owners may speak, keep comments to about three minutes and stick to Covenants 1 and 19.

coming_up.title: Rules Committee
coming_up.detail: The calendar no longer lists the covenant task force for this date; it now meets separately on November 19.

coming_up.title: Covenant Amendment Task Force
coming_up.detail: Moved here from November 5, where it had shared a meeting with the Rules Committee. Time and place not listed.

coming_up.title: Association Board of Directors
coming_up.detail: Saturday. Time and place not listed.

coming_up.title: Rules Committee
coming_up.detail: The calendar no longer lists the covenant task force for this date.

findings.title: Seven more covenant sections posted for comment, including assessments
findings.detail: The proposed changes page was rebuilt with Covenants 3, 9 and 10, 12, 15, 25, 26, and 29 posted for the first time. Covenant 25 would let the association set annual assessments without the original's word "reasonable" or its list of purposes. Covenant 9 requires approval to remove any tree over six feet tall or six inches thick, with possible replacement or monetary restitution. Covenant 3 drops the promise that approvals will not be unreasonable. Covenant 15 limits overnight parking of heavy vehicles. Covenant 26 has no text yet. The proposals for Covenants 1, 19, and 28 are unchanged.

findings.title: Covenant task force meeting moved to November 19
findings.detail: The association's calendar now lists November 5 and December 3 as Rules Committee meetings only, and gives the Covenant Amendment Task Force its own meeting on Thursday, November 19. No time or place is listed.

findings.title: Covenant rewrite still open for comment, no deadline posted
findings.detail: The association's proposed changes page was unchanged as of October 17, and it still gives no feedback deadline and no adoption or vote process. Comments can still shape Covenants 1 and 19; see Take action at the top.

findings.title: Firewise meeting held October 13
findings.detail: The association's calendar shows a Firewise (wildfire safety) meeting on October 13. Wildfire risk is the likely reason for the Covenant 1 rewrite, which would ban all outdoor fires without the association's written approval.
